title: Agent Swarm
subtitle: A self-hosted, multi-host runtime where tools are the platform and agents are compositions

lede: Every new agent an organisation adds tends to arrive with its own tooling, its own permissions and its own messaging, and every one of those is a new place for something to go wrong. I wanted to build the safety machinery once, make it the only path, and make adding an agent a matter of declaring one. Agent Swarm is that runtime. Tools are the platform: every action any agent takes passes through one frozen, tested pipeline. The runtime runs coding, analysis and service agents on local open-source models and on frontier models, spans more than one machine, and its persona library and container launcher start the seats of my governance platform.
quote: I froze the pipeline order. Less flexibility, and exactly one way an action happens.
evidence: Agent orchestration: a self-hosted multi-host agent runtime where every tool call passes one frozen pipeline of 12 steps, and a new agent persona is a declaration.
Test-gated tool catalogs: 40 declarative tools, none without golden and attack fixtures, with 50 golden fixtures in the catalog and hash-pinned catalogs checked for drift on every host.

Sandboxing and container hardening: a persona launcher of about 23,000 lines starting sandboxed containers with scoped tokens, workspaces and budgets; secrets released per action and never written to disk.
Distributed agent messaging: signed agent-to-agent envelopes with chain-depth checks, checked locally for sub-millisecond peer authorisation, and heartbeats that reclaim work from a silent agent.
Least-privilege design for autonomous coding agents: 0 commits to the main repository across three coding-agent runs on a local model.
Architecture under written decisions: 60+ locked decisions in a 2,000-line master plan, and a carve gate that keeps product crates free of estate-specific imports.
author: Corey James
